scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 9 (Section IV-F, text on PDF pages 12-13)
scenario.description: Thermal-aware empirical redundant-TSV insertion in a 3D-NoC. Router power is derived from PARSEC switching activity, and HotSpot 6.0 gives per-router temperature. Black's-model normalized fault rates, referenced to the coolest area, set 0, 1 or 2 redundant TSVs per group via thresholds found by grid search. Results are compared at target MTTF of 1.5x, 2x and 2.5x the MTTF at the reference temperature. The paper publishes no block coordinates, dimensions or per-block watts in the text, so the scenario is a 3D reliability study, not a complete 2D thermal experiment.
scenario.architecture: 3D mesh NoC with Garnet in gem5, 64 cores (4x4x4). Each router has IaSiG fault detection and correction on its UP and DOWN ports. Each vertical connection uses 36 TSVs, built from four clusters of 8 TSVs plus a synchronization TSV. Designed in NanGate 45nm with FreePDK3D45 TSV.
scenario.workload: PARSEC benchmarks, using switching activities extracted under gem5.
scenario.operating_point: Reference temperature is the coolest area of the 3D-IC. Target MTTF is 1.5x, 2x or 2.5x MTTF at Tref (Figure 9a-c). No absolute temperatures or powers were identified in the text.

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 6.0 (steady-state vs transient mode not stated) predicts per-router temperature in a 3D NoC; gem5 with Garnet NoC supplies switching activity; Synopsys CAD tools give energy per bit; Black's-model normalized fault rate is computed from the temperatures (PDF pages 12-13, Eq. 18 on page 8)
original_setup.optimizer: Grid search over two fault-rate thresholds (theta1, theta2) that set 0, 1 or 2 redundant TSVs per TSV group (Eq. 19, PDF pages 8 and 12-14)
original_setup.controller: No thermal controller. IaSiG (Isolation and Shift in Group) is an on-line hardware TSV fault detection and correction controller built on parity check and shifting redundancy (PDF pages 4-7)
original_setup.benchmark: PARSEC benchmarks on gem5 with a 3D mesh Garnet NoC of 64 cores (4x4x4); results at target MTTF of 1.5x, 2x and 2.5x the MTTF at the reference temperature (Figure 9, PDF pages 12-13)

thermal_observable.location: Per-router temperature from HotSpot 6.0, used to compute the normalized TSV-group fault rate relative to the coolest area (reference temperature). No absolute temperature is reported in the text; the Figure 9 outputs are redundancy counts and MTTF relative to target.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Per-router and per-TSV-group temperature; normalized fault rate relative to the coolest area (Eq. 18). The system MTTF is compared with a target of 1.5x, 2x or 2.5x MTTF at Tref. No peak, mean or other numeric temperature aggregate is published.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper is a 3D-IC (4x4x4 TSV-based stack) TSV lifetime-reliability study, not a 2D chiplet or interposer thermal experiment. A 2D steady-state Studio model cannot represent the vertical layer coupling, inter-layer temperature differences or TSV thermal paths.

The paper publishes no floorplan: no block coordinates, dimensions or per-block or per-router watts. The power map and floorplan used for HotSpot are not given in the text (Step 2 on PDF page 12 only mentions them), so no same-scenario geometry and power rows can be built.

The workload is derived from PARSEC switching activity from gem5 and varies over time and by benchmark, while the thermal result is only a relative fault rate; no absolute temperature is published to compare against.

The principal contributions are the IaSiG hardware fault-detection method (parity check, isolation and shift) and the grid-search redundancy insertion. These are digital reliability mechanisms with WCET in cycles, not thermal management controllers or optimizers, and do not map to a Studio thermal controller or placement optimizer.

The cooling configuration, package and HotSpot 6.0 parameters (layer stack, TSV thermal modelling, heat sink, ambient) are not published in the paper. The paper notes TSV insertion slightly changes temperature but ignores it.

The reliability metric (Black's-model normalized fault rate and MTTF, Eq. 17-18) and its parameters (Ea, current density exponent) are outside a thermal solver and are not reproduced by a steady-state temperature calculation.
